newsitem.title: USA: U.S. T-bond jumps 1-1/4 point on durables, ECI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-bond jumps 1-1/4 point on durables, ECI.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices advanced on Tuesday after the government released friendlier than expected data on first-quarter employment costs and March durable goods orders, traders said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose as much as 1-1/4 points after the data were reported, before trimming its gain a bit to a 1-5/32 jump to 95-4/32, yielding 7.02 percent.
The government said its Employment Cost Index (ECI) rose just 0.6 percent in the first quarter, less than the 0.9 percent rise that economists had forecast.

Durable goods orders in March, which economists had expected to be flat, fell 3.0 percent, while February orders, originally reported as having been up 1.5 percent, were revised to just a 0.8 percent increase.

"The market is in the process of reducing the odds for a Fed tightening in May, but by no means has eliminated that possibility," said Patrick Dimick, trader and Treasury strategist at UBS Securities Inc.

"The very good news on the ECI was concentrated in the benefits component of the ECI, which rose just 0.1 percent, the smallest rise since the first quarter of 1996," said Dimick. "The good news in the ECI report was reinforced by a larger than expected drop in durable goods orders for March."
